dedupe_keys.name: pm2 5 concentration and composition in subway systems of the northeastern united states nyu

description: This dataset, described in a 2021 Environmental Health Perspectives article by Luglio, Vilcassim and colleagues and listed in the NYU Data Catalog, measures air quality in the subway systems of four northeastern US cities. Coverage: 71 stations on 12 transit lines in New York City (MTA, PATH and LIRR; 35 platforms in 30 stations known for high PM2.5), Boston, Philadelphia and Washington DC, sampled at rush hours; Philadelphia in 2015 and the others between June and September 2019. Real-time PM2.5, black carbon and relative humidity were measured on platforms and near station entrances for 5 to 10 minutes, with particle composition (total, organic and elemental carbon, iron and silicon) and onboard concentrations between stops; gravimetric data and humidity were used to correct the real-time readings. Format and access: access by a data request form evaluated by the corresponding author. Licence and cost: on request. Caveats: short samples at selected stations, and file formats are not stated. The platform and in-train concentrations can set commuter exposure in subway ventilation and health exposure models. It relates to MTA open data and the Shanghai subway particulate matter study in the catalogue.
